populations.rationale: Tier 5 is the start of the mid-to-late transition ramp. Opening the room with 2 enemies at the first spawn point signals escalating pressure without front-loading the hardest encounter; the player can build Gnarly Rank here before the density peaks later in the room.

Second enemy marker keeps the ramp consistent — two enemies again sustains the pressure established at marker_0. Pairing these two markers as equal-density beats gives the player a rhythm to adapt to before heavier markers arrive, supporting the build side of the Gnarly Rank cycle.

Placed between the opening enemy cluster and the denser back half, this pickup serves as a deliberate breather reward. At Tier 5, pickups become scarcer, so offering one mid-room is intentional pacing — it lets the player potentially recover before the harder encounter ahead, and creates a moment where Gnarly Rank could reset (from damage) right before a potential rebuild.

This is the room's difficulty peak. Tier 5 ceiling is 3; a non-combat-heavy linear room should reach but not exceed that ceiling at its climax. Three enemies here is the intended stress spike — the player's Gnarly Rank built across marker_0 and marker_1 could be tested to a full reset here, directly serving the GDD Section 7 build-and-reset rhythm.

Stepping back down to 2 enemies after the 3-enemy spike at marker_3 creates a tension arc rather than a flat wall of maximum density. This is still above early-room norms, keeping late-room pressure, but avoids the entire back half being max-ceiling, which would blur the climax at marker_3.

Leaving the final enemy marker empty serves two purposes: it prevents combat fatigue from filling every slot in a linear, non-combat-heavy room, and it gives the player a moment to breathe and reset before exiting to the next room. A fully packed room at Tier 5 (without the combat-heavy flag) would front-load density that should belong to Tiers 6-8, disrupting the overall difficulty curve.

At Tier 5, pickups are becoming scarcer per the difficulty curve. One pickup (marker_2) is already placed; a second would over-reward the player in a room that should feel pressured. Leaving this empty reinforces that pickups are a fading luxury as the run progresses, setting expectations correctly for the harder Tier 6-8 rooms ahead.
